finding.affected: POSIX reads of the current history, rotated history and kept details
finding.before: The POSIX history readers checked file type and, on macOS, ACLs, but accepted readable regular files owned by another user or with multiple hard links. If another user could place such a file in the configured location, local history and dashboard reports could include untrusted records. The Windows opener already checked ownership and link count.

fix.invariant: Validate regular-file type, current user ownership and exactly one link on the opened descriptor before parsing bytes. The current and rotated history and kept details use the same read opener. The ownership and link check is shared with write validation, without its permission changes.
fix.behavior: An unsafe history file causes a read error. Unsafe details are reported as unreadable and are omitted from the dashboard. The same validation applies if the history lock cannot be taken. Existing Windows ownership checks, POSIX ACL checks and symlink and FIFO protections are retained.

regressions.before: Both new test methods failed on dd38e49 when ownership was simulated as foreign. The current and rotated logs were both accepted and kept details were returned.
regressions.after: Both tests passed. They cover current and rotated summaries, simulated foreign ownership, real hard links to synthetic files, the history lock fallback, and omission of unsafe details from the dashboard. Valid single-link files remain readable and mode 0644 remains unchanged on read.

verification.syntax_and_imports: Passed AST parsing of the three changed Python files and imports of history, dashboard and CLI.
verification.full_suite_coverage: Both runs included Android and real MCP SDK 1.30.0 tests. The 17 skips were Windows-specific tests.

linux_follow_up.method: Streamed only committed package source and the three related test modules into a new container. Created every fixture inside the container. Both fixture users and the reader were non-root. Foreign-owned files were created by the second UID, and link counts were verified on real filesystem entries. All target files had mode 0644. Each case checked UID, GID, link count and mode again after the calls.
linux_follow_up.case_summary: All nine cases passed. Current and rotated history failures produced a read error and no dashboard page. Kept detail failures left the summary page available, showed the unreadable notice, and omitted the detail contents. Target file metadata matched before and after every case.
linux_follow_up.cleanup: Removed the temporary container with its fixtures and verified it was absent.
linux_follow_up.scope: The Linux follow-up ran the ownership matrix and focused suites. The full Python suites above are from the earlier macOS run.

remaining: Native Windows CI for the fix commit was not run.
The macOS regression simulates a foreign owner and uses real hard links. The Linux follow-up uses different real UIDs inside the container.
The history storage caveat for macOS volumes that ignore ownership remains separately tracked in vulnerability-check-2026-11-18.json.
